Stage 3 · Grammar

Grammar

There's a kitchen · There are two bedrooms
FormExample
There's a … (one)There's a kitchen.
There are … (many)There are two bedrooms.
Is there …?Is there a garden? — Yes, there is.
  • One thing → There's a (There is a): There's a bathroom.
  • Many things → There are + number: There are three rooms.
  • Where is it? Use in, on, next to, near, on the left / right.
  • Ask: Where do you live? — I live in a flat. Where's the kitchen?

→ Present Simple (I live / she lives) comes in Lesson 9.

🔧 Build it yourself
  • 🔧 Build it yourself
  • Build it: one sofa → There IS a sofa. Two chairs → There ARE two chairs.
  • ⚠ Есть… / …бар → there is / there are. Choose by the NUMBER of things: is = one, are = many.

Stage 5 · Listening

Listening

Listen. Then choose True or False.

You can listen again.

🔊 My street — Oxford Navigate audiolisten, then answer
1The house is at number 36.
2Charlie is a waiter.
3Linda is a teacher.
4The neighbours at 34 have got a dog.
5The dog is called Benji.
6The neighbours at 38 are university students.
7Six people live at number 38.
8The students have got a cat.
Why these answers

House at 36. At 34: Charlie (waiter), Linda (nurse), two children, a dog Benji. At 38: six university students, no pets.

Stage 6 · Speaking

Your turn

Write two short lines: where you live, and one room.

When you finish, open the model answer and check yourself.

Model answer

I live in a flat in the city. There's a small kitchen and two bedrooms. There isn't a garden.

Check yourself:

  • Did you use I live in …?
  • Did you use There's a / There are …?
  • Did you name a room or place?
Talk to Sam. Answer with the words from this lesson.

Read each message. Tap 🔊 to hear Sam.

Sam

Hi again! I'm Sam. 👋

Sam

Where do you live?

Sam

Sam

Is there a garden?

Sam

Cool! 🌳

Sam

Listen: “There are a kitchen.” 🤔

Why

One thing → There's a (there is a). There are is for many: There are two rooms.

Sam

Yes! “There's a kitchen.” Great catch. 🌟

Feedback

Well done: you said where you live and fixed there is / there are. Next time, say it out loud too.
